clue.text: Chicken fighting, punching fish

indicators.note: one thing punching another drives into it, so the fighting word goes inside the fish

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish
nations fighting are at war

explanation.surface: A fish is being thumped in some cockfight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' looks like a bird in the ring, but it is the definition: a coward is a chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone chicken is slang for saying they lack courage, a timid person.

clue.text: Geriatric ultimately too old for publicity

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word geriatric

parts.note: someone past the permitted age limit is overage

explanation.surface: An elderly person turns out, in the end, to be past it for media attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Media coverage is the attention or publicity a story receives in the press.

clue.text: Snake and cat, say, in jacket

parts.note: to snake is to wind, as a path winds

indicators.note: say signals that the cat's name is to be heard, not written

parts.note: the cheetah is a big cat

explanation.surface: A serpent and a feline are tucked into a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat, say' could read as an example marker, but here 'say' means spoken: CHEETAH sounds like CHEATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A windcheater is a British name for a light windproof jacket, a windbreaker.

clue.text: Route travelled, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase tells us the past-tense verb is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to have ridden or travelled is to have rode, the past tense of ride

explanation.surface: A way taken, judging by the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a route along which traffic passes.

clue.text: Spanish food given to artist — dig in!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in tells us the digging word sits inside the other letters

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's standard artist
to till the ground is to dig it

explanation.surface: A Spanish dish is handed to a painter with an invitation to tuck in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dig in!' reads as an invitation to eat the food, but the exclamation is wordplay, not a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is a Spanish omelette of egg and potato, a classic dish of Spain.

clue.text: Surgeon beginning to observe a report that's unreliable

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the word observe
an unreliable account cannot be trusted as it stands, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written as part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A doctor starts watching, and an account given turns out to be dubious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unreliable' rearranges O (the start of 'observe'), A and REPORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon operates on patients, so the person at the operating table is an operator.

clue.text: A couple of kings, utterly drunk, discuss matters seriously

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a new order

parts.note: K is chess shorthand for king, so two kings are KK
taken as written as part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Two monarchs, completely plastered, try to have a sober conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges A, KK and UTTERLY together.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk turkey is an idiom meaning to speak frankly and get down to business.

clue.text: Private place in short where European beheaded

indicators.note: a beheaded word loses its first letter

parts.note: a Slav is a European of Slavic stock

explanation.surface: A private spot where someone from Europe lost their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' takes the first letter off SLAV. 'in short' belongs to the definition: the answer is an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Lav is a short form of lavatory, a toilet being the most private room.

clue.text: Old queen entertaining old bit on the side?

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest holds them within, so the second word sits inside the first

parts.note: Anne was Queen of Great Britain in the early 1700s
ex is a prefix meaning former or old

explanation.surface: A former monarch keeping a former lover, a bit of something on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit on the side' hints at an affair, but it is a building extension.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extra building attached at the side of a main one.

clue.text: Ship launcher viewed through the lens

indicators.note: something viewed through a lens lies within it, so the letters are inside the words

explanation.surface: Someone who launched a vessel seen through the camera.
explanation.walkthrough: Helen of Troy had 'the face that launched a thousand ships', in Marlowe's line.
explanation.definitionFit: The beauty of Helen of Troy caused the Greek fleet to sail, so she launched ships.

clue.text: Sail around track in superior position

indicators.note: around tells us the sail word goes outside the track word

parts.note: a windmill's sail is a vane
to tag someone is to track or follow them closely

explanation.surface: A boat sailing round a racecourse with the advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: A vantage point is a place giving a superior view or advantage.

clue.text: Wake, as it happens, in centre of Chennai

indicators.note: in places the broadcast word inside the central letters
centre of picks the middle three letters of the city name

parts.note: a broadcast shown as it happens is live

explanation.surface: Waking up during live events in the middle of an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of CHENNAI is ENN.
explanation.definitionFit: To wake something up, giving it life and energy, is to liven it up.

clue.text: Sweet music?

definitions.meaning: a hard stick of seaside candy, a British confection
a genre of loud guitar-led popular music

explanation.walkthrough: Seaside rock is a stick of hard candy sold at British resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock is both a seaside stick of hard candy and a form of pop music.

clue.text: Spot container on plate by unusual spot marker?

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters are in an odd order and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written as part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written as part of the letters to rearrange
on treasure maps X marks the spot

explanation.surface: A dish holding a spot sits next to an odd marker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges ON, PLATE and BY.
explanation.definitionFit: On a football pitch the penalty area encloses the penalty spot, so it contains the spot.

clue.text: Capital getting busier as one circulates

indicators.note: circulates suggests the letters moving round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written as part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written as part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A city becomes more crowded as one person goes around.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Argentina is Buenos Aires.

clue.text: Ship transported lace into truck

indicators.note: into places the rearranged lace inside the truck

parts.note: a tipper is a truck that tips its load

indicators.note: transported means carried away, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A ship's lace cargo was loaded into a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' rearranges LACE to EACL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea clipper was a fast sailing ship carrying tea from China.

clue.text: Nag at nagger's heart?

parts.note: the central letters of nagger are G and G, which spoken aloud are two gees

explanation.surface: Is the core of a nagging person a nag?
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of NAGGER is GG; spell the letter names out and you have the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee-gee is a child's word for a horse, and a nag is an old horse.

clue.text: Bound to take in a child away from home

indicators.note: to take in means to contain, so the single letter goes inside the boundary word

parts.note: a bound is a boundary or border

explanation.surface: A limit must embrace a child who lives far from their family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like a verb (obliged, or leaping) but is the noun meaning limit.
explanation.definitionFit: A boarder is a pupil who lives at a boarding school during term.

clue.text: The weakest should save money — that's basic

definitions.note: adjective in the clue; the answer is a noun, a basic element

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe within, so the coin goes inside

parts.note: the runt is the weakest of a litter
a dime is a US ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: The feeblest ought to put cash aside, which is fundamental.
explanation.definitionFit: A rudiment is a fundamental first principle of a subject.

clue.text: End of four months about perfect, more sunny

indicators.note: about means around, so the end letters surround the word for perfect

parts.note: September to December all end in -ber
right means correct or perfect

explanation.surface: The close of the year's last months is near ideal and brighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of four months' is BER, the ending shared by September, October, November and December.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighter weather is weather with more sunshine.

clue.text: Second taken to interrupt drink in bank robbery

indicators.note: to interrupt something is to break into it, so the second word goes inside

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a tick is a moment or second

explanation.surface: Someone snatches a second to break off drinking during a bank raid.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick-up is an armed robbery, the robber telling victims to stick their hands up.

clue.text: Painter getting on with black, as he'd say?

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a memo
noir is French for black, as a French painter would say

explanation.surface: An artist goes along with dark tones, in his own language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as he'd say' asks for the painter's own language: Renoir was French.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: Quote me the wrong way — that's a sickener?

indicators.note: the wrong way means the words are read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote
taken as written

explanation.surface: Misquoting me is enough to make anyone feel ill.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a substance that causes vomiting, so it makes you sick.

clue.text: Card game with an alcoholic taste?

definitions.meaning: a game of melding sets and runs of cards
tasting of the spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is whimsical: rum plus -y.
explanation.definitionFit: Rummy is a card game, and playfully means tasting of rum.

clue.text: Caribbean island rolling in it with outstanding brand

indicators.note: read as out-standing: the brand stands outside the other letters

parts.note: a marque is a brand, especially of car

indicators.note: rolling suggests the letters tumbling into a new order

explanation.surface: A rich person with a top label lives on a Caribbean isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like praise for the brand; it puts MARQUE outside TINI, which 'rolling' makes from IN IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Martinique is a French island in the Lesser Antilles of the Caribbean.

clue.text: Old dynasty, one biting back

indicators.note: back means the word for the biter is read backwards

parts.note: a gnat is an insect that bites

explanation.surface: An ancient ruling family with someone sinking teeth in from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tang dynasty ruled China from 618 to 907.

clue.text: Piece of cake but no icing? Just a bit?

indicators.note: icing goes on top, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: a piece of cake is something easy, a cinch

explanation.surface: A slice of cake without frosting, only a small amount.
explanation.walkthrough: The icing sits on top of a cake, so losing it means losing the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a small distance, so moving an inch is moving just a little.

clue.text: Tramp spoiling parties

indicators.note: spoiling suggests the letters are messed up and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A vagrant ruins the festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a noun, a vagrant, but it is the verb, to walk wearily.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily or reluctantly, to trudge.

clue.text: Within local, lager is everything

indicators.note: within says the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Inside the neighbourhood pub, beer is all that matters.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is a British name for one's nearest pub.
explanation.definitionFit: All means the whole of something, every part, so it stands for everything.

clue.text: Horse boxes in front of tall tower in the Middle East

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so the horse word surrounds the little word

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
taken as written

indicators.note: front of points to the first letter of the word tall

explanation.surface: Horseboxes sit before a high tower in Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque, from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: Speed — break sticks with it

indicators.note: it breaks into the vegetable word, sitting inside it

parts.note: celery is sold and eaten in sticks
taken as written

explanation.surface: Snapping sticks fast with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticks' looks like a verb but stands for CELERY, eaten in sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is a literary word for swiftness, quickness of movement.

clue.text: Hunter's search getting out of hand

indicators.note: out of hand means out of control, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A huntsman's quest gets out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is one who pursues, like a hunter, and also a racehorse for steeplechases.
